newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNCF 1996 loss seen at 15.2 billion francs-paper.
newsitem.headline: SNCF 1996 loss seen at 15.2 billion francs-paper.

text.p: The French state-owned railways SNCF is set to announce a 1996 loss of 15.2 billion francs, some three billion more than planned, the La Tribune newspaper said on Monday.

For 1997, the Societe des Chemins de Fer Francais (SNCF) has pencilled in a loss of two billion francs, following a debt restructuring and the transfer of the infrastructure to a special company Reseau Feree de France (RFF), the paper said.
La Tribune said that the higher than expected loss for 1996 is the result of a balance sheet clean-up by new chairman Louis Gallois prior to a restructuring.
At January 1, 1997, the SNCF debt was standing at 59 billion francs against 178 billion a year earlier. This is mainly the result of the transfer of 134.2 billion francs in debts.
